column1: # AC-M1.5 fresh acceptance set classes4.tsv (PLAN 6.1, the rulings for M1's close, 2026-11-10): authored 2026-11-10 by
# blind authors from the judged tree, second-read blind and adjudicated as classes2.tsv and classes3.tsv were, and
# sealed by path and sha256 before the engine's freeze and before any engine reads it. The sixteen claimed classes,
# ten rows each, every row acceptance, ids XX21 to XX30 (classes.tsv, classes2.tsv and classes3.tsv hold XX01 to
# XX20). Ids by class: FA feature-add, BS bug-symptom, RF refactor, DL delete, TO tests-only, PF performance, NG
# non-go, QU question, NN named-name, NP named-path, VG vague, GF greenfield, CC cross-cutting, KI knowledge-id, NE
# Columns and cells as classes.tsv: id, class, unit, target, reuse, consumers, knowledge, allow, prompt; ';' separates
# alternatives any of which is right; '-' means no line of that kind is right; '*' leaves the cell unjudged; '\n' in a
# prompt is a newline. A row whose request cites a knowledge record carries a target file, never '*' (W-M1.41c,
# W-DEBT.11). Judged tree: /tmp/rk-autosteer/acm11/tree (the tree T1c indexed), the tree classes.tsv, classes2.tsv and
# classes3.tsv were authored from. This file's authors read a clone of it without its .rashomon and .pgraph
# directories (the judged tool's indexes, internal/platform/digests.go and snapshot.go): 2006 files byte-equal to the
# judged tree's, so the rule barring the index held by construction, and the authors' transcripts were searched for it
# as well (the authoring paragraph gives the count).
# The read (registered at bd6198f0 before any row of this file existed; amended in the commit that seals this file,
# before any engine reads it, to set RASHOMON_ACM11_DUMP=1): one run of TestACM15_FreshTable -v at the frozen tip
# through goslot2 (acm15_test.go sha256 59e31a4131374f63, freshSet classes4.tsv; acm15_shape3_test.go
# ae15fd4f9157505d) with RASHOMON_ACM11_DIR the tree, RASHOMON_ACM15_FRESH this file and RASHOMON_ACM11_DUMP=1, then
# read5.py (sha256 1871ab584f9f8ef6) over this file and that output: gate shape 3 with the per-class unit term under
# option 1, a row option 1 moves from naming to prose right only when opt1.py's reading and shape 3's prose rule both
# say right. The set is read once, so that run's saved output, each row's brief included, is the primary record: any
# later view of a row is taken from it, never from a second read. The dump's branch (acm15_test.go:223) runs after the
# row's four verdicts are computed and logs the brief's text and explanation; and a dump-on run on classes2.tsv and
# classes3.tsv has the same 640 verdict lines (160 rows, two lines a row, two files) and the same summary lines as the
# dump-off run at 5559e5eb, 0 differing (eq640.py, sha256 670058d4b47c7682). The dump-on run was at 9b3248ee with
# record.go and roles.go byte-equal to 5559e5eb's, the two trees differing otherwise only in three test files
# (names2_test.go, record_ladder_test.go, record_test.go), so the equality is shown at an equal engine, not at the
# frozen tip. A printer over that output is part of the read only if the sealing commit registers it by sha256; any
# other listing of it is post hoc and labelled so. Per class the unit verdict right in 7 of 10; each role 7 of 10 of
# the rows judged where at least three are judged, and over the 160 rows; gate B as W-M1.38. Each cell is quoted
# beside the all-silent brief. What it reads is AC-M1.5's result at M1's close; no row is repaired after it and no
# further set is authored for M1.
# Owed rows. Six ids carry a shape PLAN owes this file, each a known limit registered before the file existed, written
# by their class's author under every other rule, and each note begins 'owed:': FA21, a clause-initial 'skip X in U'
# asking a behaviour of U with U's name in its object (W-M1.43 ruling 4); BS21, a fix placed by a bare 'not' contrast,
# 'fix it in the A, not the B' (W-M1.43 ruling 1); PF21, a negated behaviour whose object names the unit it changes
# (W-M1.43); NE21, leave X alone, then change an aspect of X, X naming its unit (W-M1.43, NE05); NE22, two other
# units' names in the phrase of the change (W-M1.43's NE05 tie note); NE23, a record cited whose package the same
# request bars (the W-M1.43 freeze's known limit). An owed row counts in its class's ten like any other row: a miss is
# a miss, and the note only names the registered limit behind it. The close quotes each of the six by id with its
# verdict, beside its class cell. W-DEBT.11's generated-file case is owed no row: the tree holds one generated file
# (internal/budget/budgets_gen.go), and its one record, B417, is cited by classes3.tsv KI12, a taken subject. No row
# of this file exercises it: W-DEBT.11 stands as debt, untested by this file.
# Authoring (2026-11-10, Sonnet 5.5, claude-sonnet-5-5, one author per class; 17 calls, the sixteen classes and the
# vague re-author, 2,364,022 subagent tokens, 614 tool uses, 71.4 min summed over the calls, against classes3's
# 2,170,639 over 16 calls; answers out/authors.json sha256 238bf30d): each author was given the authoring rules

# its class's requests in prompts.tsv, edge.tsv, classes.tsv, classes2.tsv and classes3.tsv as taken (no repeat, no
# paraphrase, no reused subject). No author built a brief or ran the engine. The authors' ids were XX21 to XX30 as

# tool input, the non-go author's grep for '.pgraph' in the clone's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md, two text files, in

# authors were barred from the index is not verified here. The controller's scripts read the index for record nodes
# and declares edges, no agent was passed anything from it, and the consumer and knowledge truths are derived from it,
# the registered circularity limitation. Vague: both authors of the class skipped the kit's Step 2 reads. The first
# (out/first/vague.json, 4084d3e4) read no byte of atlas.txt (it ran wc -l on it) and no tree file; the re-author
# (call 17, fresh, the identical prompt prompts/author-vague.txt 4b25909e) read the first 3000 of atlas.txt's 54886
# bytes and no tree file. Step 2 cannot move a cell in this class, whose unit, target and reuse the rule fixes to '-'

# (out/authors/vague.json, 19076f3f) in this file and keeps the first beside it, unused: neither was chosen by its
# content, no third author ran and no prompt changed. Paraphrase proximity, each row's nearest taken vague row
# (classes.tsv, classes2.tsv, classes3.tsv; prompts.tsv and edge.tsv hold none) by Jaccard similarity of case-folded
# word sets, a word any run of letters or digits, ties listed (near4.py sha256 2387f25d, output 4a3d3132): VG21 0.11
# classes3 VG18 'different tack now, please'; VG22 0.12 classes3 VG11 'scrap that, start fresh'; VG23 0.09 classes3
# VG12 'nope, go back a step'; VG24 0.18 classes3 VG20 'that's wrong, loop back and redo'; VG25 0.20 classes2 VG06
# 'wrong tweak, try the other one' and classes3 VG17 'put it back the way it was'; VG26 0.09 classes.tsv K1 'fix it'
# and K10 'ship it'; VG27 0.11 classes3 VG18 'different tack now, please'; VG28 0.08 classes2 VG02 'never mind, skip
# it'; VG29 0.14 classes2 VG04 'give it one more pass'; VG30 0.17 classes.tsv K7 'that broke the build, undo it' and
# classes3 VG17 'put it back the way it was'. The measure counts shared words, not meaning: QA's reading before the
# second read named classes3 VG13 ('that's not it, flip it around') nearest to VG25 in sense, which it scores 0.09,
# and the two authors converged on each other (the first's VG22 'hmm, revert that last change', the second's 'hmm,

# Repairs at assembly, one round, before the second read. Every trigger is an instrument finding written to

# raw-r0.tsv (2b167121) to raw.tsv (faa70239), 0 cells changed outside the twelve prompts. assemble.py (28db7d46) over

# copy, identifier or count finding: no row went to the director after the round. Those four keep their authored
# units, narrower than the record's applies-to set, under classes3's reading of the knowledge-id rule (the record's

# Second read (blind, Sonnet 5.5, three readers per row given the atlas and their batch only; 48 calls, 24 unit and 24

column9: Skip a UTF-8 byte-order mark at the start of the first line the linescan reader hands back, so a transcript saved by a Windows editor still decodes its first record.
When hooks turn out to be disabled, have the check say which file set it and not only which layer, so the refusal can point at the exact path to edit.

The outcomes bundle gives me the total of fired lines, but I can't tell forty fires from one noisy session from forty sessions that each fired once. Add how many sessions contributed at least one fired line, printed under the same under-five rule as the other counts.

Purge tells me what it removed but never how much space that gave back. I want the outcome to carry the total size of the files it actually deleted, counted as they go and not guessed from the plan, so the verb can print it.

Today the only way to learn that someone edited one of our hook entries is to run watch or detach and get refused. I want a read-only check on the install side that walks the events we install into and returns, for each entry of ours that no longer matches what watch writes, the event and what differs, the same detail the refusal prints. It must not change the document, and another install's entry must never show up in it. Status can then list the edited ones without anybody attempting a removal.

When a run's saved fold gets thrown away and the Stop falls back to the full streaming read, nothing says why, because the validity check just answers false. Have it also report which check failed: the schema or writer, the records file having a new identity, or which of the four cursors went stale. Then I can tell a restored records file from a forget rewrite when I am chasing slow Stops. The yes/no behaviour and the fall-back must stay exactly as they are.

The disclosure inventory has a section for the environment variables the tool reads, but it is empty, so nothing that renders from it can tell a user which variables change behaviour. Fill it in, starting with the one that sets the store's size cap, with a one-line effect for each and not marked test-only.

Trust bindings only ever pile up. Untrust needs someone to remember the spec's path, and a binding for a repository that was deleted or moved stays forever, counting toward the size cap that makes the next trust fail with a message to untrust something first. Add a way to drop every binding whose spec file is no longer there. The existence check should go through the same file-system abstraction discovery reads through, so tests don't need a real disk, and it should report how many it dropped.

Every reader of a payload field that holds an integer ends up writing the same few lines: check the span is a number, parse its raw bytes, and return 0 on anything else. Put that on the span type in the scanner so callers stop copying it, with the same forgiving 0 for anything odd. Don't convert the existing callers in this change.

The check that keeps an agent from running consent, watch and purge only trips on one variable, so a command that unsets it first gets through; make it trip on the AI_AGENT variable Claude Code puts in its shell children too, and name whichever signal it saw in the refusal.

The instructions line in the session brief reads 1024 KiB when a project's instruction files add up to just under a megabyte, instead of rolling over to MiB. Smaller and larger sizes print fine. Fix it in the brief, not the store.

A pytest run whose output has Windows line endings, or has colour codes forced on, is never recognised as passed or failed by the gate-output reader, even though the summary banner is plainly there. The gate just ends up with no verdict. The same run with plain Linux output is classified correctly. Make the reader cope with the stray carriage returns and escape sequences so the gate goes green or red as it should.
After a compaction, the continuity note never quotes the standing instructions I gave earlier in the session, even when I had given several.
When I ask the agent about Next.js or Node.js, rashomon decides I named a file and then tells the agent the project has no such path. A framework name is not a path.
Giving the forget command a negative duration as its cutoff, say minus a day, wipes every record I have instead of being refused.

Editing a plain-text LICENSE or README file in a repo makes the closing line after each turn claim my build and test results are out of date, as if I had changed source. The markdown versions of the same files do not do that. Those text files should count as documentation.

The merge guard's rerun summary counts a gate as differing whenever the saved checkpoint recorded it as anything other than passed or failed. A gate that was stale or never run at checkpoint time, and now reruns green, lands in the differ tally and makes it look as if the checkpoint lied. That should be told apart from a real disagreement, where the checkpoint said green and the rerun is red or the other way round. Keep the printed line format as it is.

The scrub tool for captured payloads rewrites my home directory to a tilde even where the home path only shows up in the middle of some other path. A mirrored copy under a backup folder, for instance, comes out as a mangled path with a tilde in the middle. It is meant to rewrite the home directory only where it starts a path. Paths that merely contain my home path further in should be left alone.
I hand-edited the config to turn one project's summary off with a capital O, and the Stop line still prints the value line. The notes switch treats the same kind of hand edit as off.
When two steer lines of a session share a long id prefix, the ambiguity message lists the candidates looking identical, so I cannot tell how many more characters to type.

The pair report keeps its own copy of the token-counts struct, with the same five fields and the same JSON tags as the one the spend estimate already declares for a response. Drop the duplicate and use the spend one, and make sure the pair's JSON output comes out exactly as before.
The checkpoint line reader has a public entry point that does nothing but forward to a private function with a different name, so collapse them into one function and fix every caller.

The file that holds the steering message templates has grown to well over 700 lines, because the table of later-prompt rows and the small table of rows that carry an approved lesson as their last line both sit in it, beside the binding structs and the first table. The wrapped, symbols and continuity variants already each have a file of their own. Move those two tables out the same way so each family of rows lives in one place, without touching a single template id or format string. The rendering tests must stay green untouched.

When I read the code that assembles a session's report input, the transcript reading (the ids of the main and subagent files, the final assistant text, the missing-file check) takes up the bottom third of the file, far from the store reading that it is unrelated to. Pull the transcript-reading functions into their own separate file in that package; what they return and when they are called must not change.

The consent record and the harness answers are both written through a private helper that opens a temp file beside the target, chmods it, writes, syncs and renames, and the store already exports a shared function that does exactly that. Switch our writer onto the store's one and delete the local copy. The files left on disk must be the same.

Every time we add a rung to the task-preflight note ladder we have to edit a pile of long signatures: the function that builds each rung's message and the one that builds its recorded form both take eight positional arguments, and the first-prompt and later-prompt binding builders repeat most of them. Group the values that travel together (the preflight lists, the symbols line, the brief, the item count, the unknowns flag, the riding lesson and the digest function) into one small struct and pass that instead. The messages it prints and the steer line it records must stay byte for byte the same, and the existing tests in the package should pass as they are.
Break the stdin payload reader up, since the shortcut for an already-buffered reader, the chunked read loop and the garbage collection after a big read are all tangled in one long function.
Collapse the two ledger openers in the lessons verbs, one read-write and one read-only, into a single opener that takes a read-only flag.

The function that works out the hook-entry and probe state for a coverage record is just called resolve, and there are several other resolves around the repo that mean something else entirely (the baseline's, the intent's). Rename it so the name says it is about coverage, and update its callers.

In the lesson ledger's main file the lifecycle (open, import, approve, withdraw, save) shares space with the state signing: the manifest HMAC over the three state files, the digest helper and the creation of the ledger's key. Reading a change to the ledger means scrolling past that bookkeeping, and the prompt-path reader uses the same signing code. Move the signing and key code out into a separate new file in that package. Keep the manifest bytes identical so ledgers that exist today still verify, and do not change who calls what.

The spend estimate counts responses that ran in fast mode and prints a note saying they bill at a premium we don't price. We don't use fast mode on this account, so that counting and the note are just noise. Take the fast-mode tally out of the estimate, the JSON field included, and leave the closing out-of-scope line as it is.

In the recap line for a gate whose last run was inside a wrapper like make, there is a special sentence for the case where the call printed its own exit status. Drop that special case so every wrapped run whose output was not read just says the output names no run.
Take the line about corrections kept from before the install out of the session brief, along with whatever reads the kept record just to build it.

There is a hard-coded list of package registries and GitHub hosts that are supposed to never count as novel hosts for a project, plus an exported function that checks a hostname against it. I went looking for who uses it and nothing does: the novelty lines are built from the stored per-project hosts alone, so the list only misleads anyone reading the code. Delete the list and the checker together with the comment that explains them. Keep how a baseline file is read, folded and saved exactly the same.

The re-anchor tool for the perf budgets has a --kind flag that narrows --all and --provisional to only benchmark rows or only RSS rows. Nobody has passed it since the first anchoring; people either name rows with --rows or take everything for the platform. I would like it gone, together with the validation of its value and the filtering it drives, so the selection is always every matching row of both kinds. The usage text and the long doc comment at the top should stop mentioning it too, and the wrapper script that forwards arguments needs no change.

The digest command takes the last assistant message either from stdin or from a command-line flag that exists only so a person can drive it by hand. Argv is visible to every process of the user, and nothing real passes it that way. Remove the flag and keep the stdin route working as it does.
Nobody shares lesson files between teams here, so drop the import subcommand of the learn command, its usage text and the code behind it.

We have two answers to which git work tree a directory sits in: one walks up looking for a .git entry, and the other in the store resolves symlinks on the nearest existing ancestor first. Get rid of the copy purge carries and make the purge confirmation use the store's.
Remove the line on the short screen that tells someone their earlier agreement predates the current scope; the full screen can keep saying it.

The lesson ledger has a candidate gate: a function that decides from a count of episodes, sessions, days and contradictions whether a mined pattern may enter at proposed, with its own evidence struct and minimum constants. Nothing calls it in the product, and there is no miner producing that evidence anywhere in the tree. Delete the gate with the struct and the three floors that exist only for it. The tier thresholds and the Wilson bound that move a lesson between tiers have to stay as they are.

A lesson that got demoted is meant to come back to probation by itself once its evidence recovers, but I can't find a test that walks one down and then back up. Can you add one that starts with a tally whose upper bound sits under the cutoff, then keeps adding confirmed labels until it clears, and checks the tier after each step? Test only, the tier logic stays as it is.

I want a test that when the hook's stdin was too big to buffer, the harness check never tells the entry to stand down, even if the leftover bytes happen to look like another harness's payload. Otherwise an oversized Claude Code payload would silently lose its too-large coverage reason.
Add tests showing that the test-command guesser reads nothing from CI lines that pipe, background the job or use a substitution, so those stay unknown instead of guessed.

The check that decides whether a saved fold is still a safe place to resume a session from has a few quiet ways to go wrong, and I only see tests for the obvious ones. I'd like cases where the saved position is inside the file but the byte just before it is not a line break, where the file has been rewritten shorter than the size the cursor remembers, and where one of the secondary files is missing entirely while its cursor is at zero versus past zero. Each case should say whether the fold is accepted or sent back to the full re-read. No change to product code, and keep the existing tests green.

The commit receipt finds the newest checkpoint by walking run directories, and only the report's best-effort walk is supposed to stop at a cap and say it was cut short, while the trailer lookup walks everything. Add a test that builds a store with more run directories than the cap and checks that the capped query reports truncation and the uncapped latest lookup still returns the newest checkpoint. Tests only.
Add a test that the removal plan for a store leaves alone a symlink sitting where a run file should be, and never plans to delete whatever it points at.
